steps.text:
**Best chart type: Clustered (grouped) column chart with a secondary line series (combo chart)** ### Why this works for your data | Aspect of the data | How the chart shows it best | |--------------------|----------------------------| | **Two categorical dimensions** – *region* and *month* | The X‑axis can list the four regions (North, South, East, West). Within each region, two adjacent columns represent the two months (Jan, Feb). This “clustered” layout lets you compare the same month across regions and also see the month‑over‑month change within each region. | | **Two numerical measures** – *units* and *revenue* | Plot **units** as the height of the columns (primary Y‑axis). Add **revenue** as a line (or a second set of columns) using a secondary Y‑axis. This lets you see the relationship between volume and monetary result without one measure dwarfing the other (revenue numbers are roughly {{int:8:12}}‑{{int:24:36}}× larger than units). | | **Trend over time** | Because the months are ordered inside each region, you can instantly spot increases or drops from Jan → Feb for each region. | | **Easy to read** | Viewers can compare:
• *Across regions* for a given month (e.g., “Which region sold the most units in Feb?”)
• *Across months* within a region (e.g., “Did revenue rise from Jan to Feb in the West?”)
• *Units vs. revenue* relationship (e.g., “High units don’t always equal high revenue – see South’s drop in Feb”). | ### Quick visual description ``` Units (bars) Revenue (line) ^ ┌───┐ ┌───┐ ┌───┐ ┌───┐ ┌───┐ ┌───┐ ┌───┐ ┌───┐ | │ │ │ │ │ │ │ │ │ │ │ │ │ │ | │ │ │ │ │ │ │ │ │ │ │ │ │ │ | └─┬─┘ └─┬─┘ └─┬─┘ └─┬─┘ └─┬─┘ └─┬─┘ └─┬─┘ └─┬─┘ | │Jan │Feb │Jan │Feb │Jan │Feb │Jan │Feb +---------------------------------------------------------------► North South East West ``` - **Columns** (blue) = *units* for Jan & Feb, grouped by region. - **Line** (red, right‑hand Y‑axis) = *revenue* for Jan & Feb, points connected across months. ### Implementation tip Most spreadsheet or BI tools (Excel, Google Sheets, Power BI, Tableau, etc.) let you create a **Combo Chart**: 1. Insert a **Clustered Column** chart with *region* on the X‑axis and *units* as the column values, split by *month*. 2. Add a **Line** series for *revenue* and assign it to a secondary Y‑axis. 3. Format the secondary axis (currency) and give the chart a clear title, e.g., “Units Sold and Revenue by Region and Month”. This visual will give you an immediate, at‑a‑glance comparison of both metrics across the two dimensions you care about.
